description: A mountain valley worn by rain, as a terrain for a game engine. The ground is a heightfield of 257 × 257 samples over size × size metres: a valley winding along X between walls of ridged mountains, from 0 at the lowest point of the river bed to height at the highest ridge. Rain wears it in three steps, all scaled by erosion (0 leaves the ground raw): gullies are cut where the water gathers on the walls (heightfield_flow), sediment fans are laid where they reach the floor, and droplet erosion (heightfield_erode) wears the whole ground and settles what it carries. The river follows the valley's centre line on a bed that falls all the way from the high end (+X) to the low end (-X), river_depth below the floor, and is carved into the ground. Layers: flow (0..1, the water draining through each sample, on a log scale), sediment (metres of fans and settled material) and river (0..1 under the river). The river output is that bed as a curve; the preview is the ground as a mesh with a colour map painted from the layers: grass (fresher where water gathers), rock on the slopes, darker gullies, pale fans and dark water in the river. Asserts check that the ground stays between 0 and height and that the river never rises along its course.

height.label: height
height.desc: from the valley floor to the highest ridge (m)

erosion.label: erosion
erosion.desc: how long the rain wears the ground; 0 leaves it raw

river_depth.label: river depth
river_depth.desc: how deep the river cuts into the valley floor (m)

seed.label: seed
seed.desc: changes the mountains, not the look

params.expression:
// the fans as sediment in metres: the more rain, the thicker
erosion * 5 * cell * clamp(2 * sediment, 0, 1)

no_debris.note: one node per layer: heightfield_layer delete takes a single layer name, and a space-separated list silently deletes nothing

params.expression:
// pale where sediment lies thick on gentle ground: the fans
smoothstep(2 * cell, 3.5 * cell, sediment) * (1 - rock)

colour_map.note: heightfield_to_tex puts the -Z row at the top of the image while heightfield_to_mesh gives -Z the uv v = 0 (the bottom): mirrored in v, the map lands on its own samples; drop this once the two agree

terrain.label: Terrain
terrain.description: The eroded ground from 0 to height, 257 × 257 samples, with the layers flow, sediment and river.

river.label: River
river.description: The river's course along the valley floor, on its bed, falling all the way from the high end to the low end.

preview.label: Preview
preview.description: The terrain as a mesh with a colour map painted from its layers: rock on the slopes, grass on the floor, darker gullies, pale sediment fans and water in the river.
